---
title: "Glossary"
---

Terms used across the Manifold course. Runtime vocabulary aligns with
the [Phase 7 constructive-realization contract](../../templates/README.qmd).
For Pico-side vocabulary (Rule, Parser, Composer, Pico), see the
[Pico course glossary](../pico/glossary.html). For composition
vocabulary (XRD, Composition, XR, Managed Resource), see the
[Crossplane course glossary](../crossplane/glossary.html).

## Channel
A named runtime pathway that carries typed values between Elements
inside an `InteractionTopology`. In this course, one Wrangler-declared
Channel wires exactly one event into the hosted Pico. The Channel is
the wire; it is not the payload.

## Control Surface
An operator- or learner-facing interface that expresses OperatorIntent
against declared runtime state. In this course the Control Surface is
a small **Python CLI-style shell command** (`kubectl exec` /
`curl`) that sends one event onto the Channel. Graphical Control
Surfaces (for example, Home Assistant) are out of scope.

## Event
A single value delivered onto a Channel. Under the Phase 7 contract an
event conforms to an `EventType` — described here in prose and a small
inline shape rather than a formal schema.

## EventType
The typed contract for values carried by a Channel. In this course the
only `EventType` is `hello.request`, a small JSON-shaped payload
carrying a `value` field that the hosted Pico echoes back on its log.

## InteractionTopology
A declarative description of which Elements interact through which
Channels within a `RuntimeEnvironment`. In this course the topology is
minimal: one Pico and one Channel, authored as a small Wrangler-style
YAML fragment shipped with the lab.

## Manifold
The **RuntimeEnvironment** taught in this course. Manifold hosts Pico
Elements on a Kubernetes RuntimeSubstrate and owns their lifecycle and
notification path. Manifold does not replace Kubernetes, Crossplane,
or Sandcastle — it sits on top of them.

## Observation
A runtime-captured fact about an Element's behaviour inside a
RuntimeEnvironment. In this course the single Observation is the one
log line the hosted Pico prints in response to the one event sent onto
its Channel. Observations feed Phase 2 `feedback[]`.

## OperatorIntent
A declaration of desired runtime state expressed through a Control
Surface. In this course the OperatorIntent is: "send one
`hello.request` event to the hosted Pico via channel `hello`, and
capture the response."

## Pico engine
The in-process host, inside Manifold, that actually runs a Pico
Element. The Pico engine consumes events from a Channel and produces
Observations. It is the runtime counterpart of the `hello-world-pico`
artifact produced by the [Hello Pico lab](../../labs/hello-pico/index.qmd).

## RuntimeEnvironment
A concrete environment hosted on the RuntimeSubstrate in which Pico
Elements execute and interact. In this course the RuntimeEnvironment
is **Manifold**, deployed onto a local minikube cluster. A
RuntimeEnvironment runs *on* the RuntimeSubstrate; it does not replace
it.

## RuntimeSubstrate
The underlying execution layer that hosts every runtime Element in the
academy. In this course, and across the Hello Pico roadmap, the
RuntimeSubstrate is always **Kubernetes** (concretely, minikube).

## Wrangler
The **InteractionTopology authoring** surface. Wrangler outputs a
declarative topology (Channels, subscriptions, children) that
Manifold applies over the runtime. Wrangler is not the runtime; it is
an additional declarative input to the same Realization chain.
